Please read /papers/investigations-5/10_riemann_siegel_critical_time/notes/01_RSCT_CONTINUATION_AND_PROMPT_20261111.md, and continue the research there.  

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder. Please provide guidance for the continuation at the end of your research, and a continuation note for model changes, also mentioning the suggested continuation model in the chat.

I’ll read the continuation note and the project’s established results, then pursue the next research step. I’ll save progress, research notes, and continuation guidance in the investigation’s folders and keep this chat history current.

The previous pass found that the test at heights 4, 6, and 8 cannot rule out a double zero at large centers. I’m examining whether moving the observations toward the real axis gives a useful test, and what happens to the full arithmetic formula and its error bounds at that scale.

The formula remains controllable when the observation distance is proportional to \(1/\log a\), provided both reflected arms are retained. But the earlier one-arm zeta comparison no longer applies there. I’ve also derived an event-conditioned expansion; I’m checking whether its full arithmetic sum can be bounded usefully after the event’s vanishing value and derivative are removed.

The calculation gives a precise limit: subtracting the event’s value and derivative reduces the absolute bound by \((\log a)^2\), but that bound still grows like \(a^{\,1/4-c/16}/(\log a)^2\). The approximation error itself tends to zero. What remains unproved is a favorable sign from the correlated arithmetic terms; the growing bound does not prove that the signed sum is large.

The bounded research pass and handoff are saved. The checks found no broken local links or changed inputs from the earlier reviewed passes. The next step is to find a signed-correlation estimate that uses the event equations; further absolute-bound refinements are unlikely to help. I recommend GPT-6 Astra for that conceptual work. Chat capture is current, and I’m arranging capture of the final reply.

Completed the bounded **RSCT-B01 r4** continuation.

The complete formula remains controllable at distances proportional to \(1/\log a\), with an absolute approximation error tending to zero. Subtracting the event’s vanishing value and derivative improves the termwise bound by \((\log a)^2\), but that bound still grows. **No zero-exclusion result was obtained**; the missing step is a favorable sign from the correlated arithmetic terms. Checking was same-assistant only.

Saved:

- [Research derivation](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/10_riemann_siegel_critical_time/notes/06_RSCT_B01_R4_MICROSCOPIC_EVENT_EXPANSION_20261111.md)
- [Updated progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/10_riemann_siegel_critical_time/research-progress/01_RSCT_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261111.md)
- [Continuation and model-change handoff](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/10_riemann_siegel_critical_time/notes/01_RSCT_CONTINUATION_AND_PROMPT_20261111.md)

Next, test a specific signed-correlation estimate using the event equations. **Suggested continuation model: [GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra)**; reserve GPT-6.1 Sol for execution once a concrete proof method is fixed.

Chat history is registered and refreshed; capture of this final reply is queued.
Please continue with RSCT-B01 r5 and test a signed-correlation estimate using the event equations. Update the research notes, progress register, chat history, and continuation guidance.

I’ll reopen RSCT-B01 for one bounded r5 pass, test a signed-correlation estimate against the event equations, and update the notes, progress register, chat history, and handoff with the result and its limits.

I’m testing a specific way to use the event equations: keep the signed cross terms, then ask whether a lower bound follows when each canonical phase is allowed to vary inside its amplitude disk. This is a broader class than the actual arithmetic phases. If the bound fails there, it will identify exactly which phase information this method cannot discard.

The proposed bound fails in that relaxed class. I found coefficients that satisfy both event equations exactly, retain the correction term, and give a negative signed quadratic value of order \(1/(\log a)^2\). This is a limitation of the disk-based estimate: the example attenuates modes and does not satisfy the actual arithmetic phase law, so it is not a canonical collision.

The r5 result and handoff are saved. They stop only the estimate based on independent amplitude disks and the two event equations; estimates using the exact magnitudes and shared logarithmic phases remain open. I’m checking the links and prior-file hashes now, then I’ll refresh the chat record and arrange capture of the final reply.

Completed **RSCT-B01 r5**.

The tested signed-correlation bound fails when actual phases are replaced by independent amplitude disks—even with both event equations imposed exactly. An explicit example retains the correction term and gives a negative value of order \(1/(\log a)^2\). **It is not a canonical collision:** it violates the exact coefficient magnitudes and shared arithmetic phase law.

For r6, test a method that explicitly uses additional canonical phase constraints. Suggested model: **[GPT-6 Astra](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra)**.

Same-assistant checking only; no new zero-exclusion result. Links and recorded input hashes passed verification. Chat history is refreshed, with this final reply’s capture queued.
